details: CONFIRMED by a scratch test that wraps relay_gate.take_worktree_lock to commit, before taking the lock, either a remote log of the head or a code
change; with the remote path the fake runner is called once in both. In run(), the Mac branch after the lock does `now = check_ready(...)`, the
license check, reusable/finished_red on `now`, and `if now != head: raise GateRefused`; _remote_gate is entered before all of that.
The worktree lock exists for exactly this race (the cycle's recovery step starts a second gate when it cannot see the first). Waste on every
such race (principle 2). Size: 15 min (move the re-check block above the remote branch, or repeat it there, plus two tests).
evidence: LOCKWAIT remote calls after a log landed meanwhile: 1
MOVED remote calls=1 refusal=the worktree changed while the gate ran (HEAD moved to 572988e3ac44 (files: lib/z.py)): commit, then run it again
failing_case: Two `relay gate` calls on one worktree with a remote host: the second waits on the worktree lock while the first finishes and commits
<H>.remote.gate.log. The second then calls remote.run again on H (scratch repro: 1 remote call after a green remote log of H was committed
during the wait), a duplicate 13-minute remote gate. Same with code committed during the wait: the remote runs the old head to the end, then
the gate is refused "the worktree changed while the gate ran (HEAD moved to 572988e3ac44 (files: lib/z.py))" (repro: remote calls=1).
The Mac path re-runs check_ready, the license check and both reuses after the wait and refuses "moved to another commit while the gate waited"
before running anything; the remote path should do the same.
fix_hint: After take_worktree_lock and before `_remote_gate`, do the same as the Mac branch: now = check_ready(worktree); re-run the license check;
reusable/finished_red on `now` with `host`; raise GateRefused when now != head. Simplest: hoist that block out of the slot try so both paths share it.
pass_cases: 1. A green remote log of H committed while the gate waits on the lock: the gate returns (0, that log) and the fake runner records no call.
2. A code commit made while the gate waits on the lock: GateRefused "...moved to another commit while the gate waited..." and the fake runner records no call.
3. A red remote log of H committed during the wait: the red is reported ("reported, not run"), no runner call.
4. No change during the wait: the runner is called once and <H>.remote.gate.log is committed (test_a_remote_gate_writes_its_own_log_and_runs_nothing_here keeps passing).
reason: tests/test_gate_remote.py Waited tests (3 failing on base) plus test_no_change_during_the_wait_runs_the_remote_once:266 pass.
findings.summary: the remote path runs right after the worktree lock with no re-check: a gate that waited runs the remote again on code that moved or that was gated meanwhile

details: CONFIRMED by a scratch test on the RemoteBase fixture (commit install.sh on main, then go(fake.remote())). _toolchain_changed runs
`git diff --name-only base HEAD -- <files>`, a two-tree diff of the default branch's tip against HEAD, so changes made on master count as the
branch's own. The design row says "the branch changes container/Containerfile, deps.toml or install.sh against the default branch" and its
reason is "no branch recipe runs with network on the server": only the branch's own recipe change matters; the printed line also says "this
branch changes". The line also says "on this Mac" twice ("its gates run on this Mac until it lands; this gate runs on this Mac"): drop the first.
evidence: TOOLCHAIN calls=[] runs=1 err="gate: this branch changes relay's toolchain (install.sh); its gates run on this Mac until it lands; this gate runs on this Mac"
git log --since=2026-09-30 --format=%h master -- install.sh deps.toml container/Containerfile | wc -l  ->  9
failing_case: A lane forked from master; master then lands a change to install.sh (9 master commits touched install.sh, deps.toml or container/Containerfile
since 30 Sep). The lane itself never touches those files. Its next build-time gate: no remote call, the Mac runs, and it prints
"gate: this branch changes relay's toolchain (install.sh); its gates run on this Mac until it lands; this gate runs on this Mac" (scratch repro:
calls=[] runs=1 with that line). It should go to the remote: the branch changed no toolchain file. Lanes take the default branch only at the
landing, so such a lane gates on the Mac for its whole life.
fix_hint: Use the three-dot form: `git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD -- <TOOLCHAIN>` (fork point to HEAD). Shorten the line to
"this branch changes relay's toolchain (install.sh) and gates on this Mac until it lands".
pass_cases: 1. Master changes install.sh after the fork, the branch does not touch it: the fake runner is called, no toolchain line.
2. The branch changes install.sh (test_a_branch_that_changes_the_toolchain_gates_on_the_mac): no runner call, the toolchain line naming install.sh.
3. The branch changes deps.toml and master changes install.sh: the line names deps.toml only.
4. The branch changes install.sh and back to master's content: no toolchain line (content equals the fork point).
reason: tests/test_gate_remote.py Details toolchain tests fail on base, pass on head.
findings.summary: the toolchain rule diffs the default branch's tip, not the fork point: a toolchain change landed on master sends every lane that has not taken it to the Mac, with a line saying the branch changed it

details: CONFIRMED by reading: `return code != 0`. The design's F7 reason is "the gate that failed is the gate that confirms the fix"; a stop or a kill is
no failure of the code. Size: 5 min.
failing_case: A build-time Mac gate stopped at the time limit under load (exit 124) or killed when the session ended (exit 143): the next gate of the branch
is kept on the Mac ("the last gate of this branch on this Mac is red"), the loaded machine, though finished_red treats exactly these exits as
"came from outside the commit". It should count only a finished red (0 < n < 127, n != 124), as finished_red does.
fix_hint: Return `0 < code < 127 and code != LIMIT_EXIT`, and skip the log (keep walking) for 124/127/>=128, or treat it as not red.
pass_cases: 1. Newest Mac log exit 124, then a gate with a remote: the runner is called.
2. Newest Mac log exit 1: no runner call, the "last gate ... is red" line (test_after_a_red_mac_log_... keeps passing).
3. Newest Mac log exit 0: the runner is called.
reason: tests/test_gate_remote.py:296 fails on base, passes on head.
findings.summary: a Mac log stopped at the time limit (124) or killed (127, >=128) counts as a red Mac gate and keeps the branch on the Mac
